{{Short description|Concept in mathematics}}
In the mathematical subject [[geometric group theory]], a '''fully irreducible automorphism''' of the [[free group]] ''F<sub>n</sub>'' is an element of [[Out(Fn)|Out(''F<sub>n</sub>'')]] which has no  periodic conjugacy classes of proper free factors in ''F<sub>n</sub>'' (where ''n''&nbsp;>&nbsp;1). Fully irreducible automorphisms are also referred to as "irreducible with irreducible powers" or "iwip" automorphisms. The notion of being fully irreducible provides a key Out(''F<sub>n</sub>'') counterpart of the notion of a [[pseudo-Anosov map|pseudo-Anosov element]] of the [[mapping class group]] of a finite type surface. Fully irreducibles play an important role in the study of structural properties of individual elements  and of subgroups of Out(''F<sub>n</sub>'').

==Formal definition==

Let <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> where <math>n\ge 2</math>. Then <math>\varphi</math> is called ''fully irreducible''<ref>Thierry Coulbois and Arnaud Hilion, ''Botany of irreducible automorphisms of free groups'', [[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]] '''256''' (2012), 291–307</ref> if there does not exist an integer <math>p\ne 0</math> and a proper free factor <math>A</math> of <math>F_n</math> such that <math>\varphi^p([A])=[A]</math>, where <math>[A]</math> is the conjugacy class of <math>A</math> in <math>F_n</math>. Equivalently, for all <math>p > 0</math> and any proper free factor <math> A </math> of <math> F_n </math>, <math> \varphi^{p}([A]) \neq [A]</math>.
Here saying that  <math>A</math> is a proper free factor of <math>F_n</math> means that <math>A\ne 1</math> and there exists a [[subgroup]] <math>B\le F_n, B\ne 1</math> such that <math>F_n=A\ast B</math>.

Also, <math>\Phi\in \operatorname{Aut}(F_n)</math> is called ''fully irreducible'' if the outer automorphism class <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> of <math>\Phi</math> is fully irreducible.

Two fully irreducibles <math>\varphi,\psi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> are called ''independent'' if <math>\langle \varphi\rangle \cap \langle \psi \rangle = \{1\}</math>.

===Relationship to irreducible automorphisms===

The notion of being fully irreducible grew out of an older notion of an "irreducible" outer automorphism of <math>F_n</math> originally introduced in.<ref name=BH92/> An element <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>, where <math>n\ge 2</math>, is called ''irreducible'' if there does not exist a free product decomposition
:<math>F_n=A_1\ast\dots \ast A_k \ast C</math>
with <math>k\ge 1</math>, and with <math>A_i\ne 1, i=1,\dots k</math> being proper free factors of <math>F_n</math>,  such that <math>\varphi</math> permutes the conjugacy classes <math>[A_1], \dots, [A_k] </math>.

Then <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> is fully irreducible in the sense of the definition above  if and only if for every <math>p\ne 0</math> <math>\varphi^p</math> is irreducible.

It is known that for any ''atoroidal'' <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> (that is, without periodic conjugacy classes of nontrivial elements of <math>F_n</math>), being irreducible is equivalent to being fully irreducible.<ref>Ilya Kapovich, ''Algorithmic detectability of iwip automorphisms''. [[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]] '''46''' (2014), no. 2, 279–290.</ref> For non-atoroidal automorphisms, Bestvina and Handel<ref name=BH92/> produce an example of an irreducible but not fully irreducible element of  <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>, induced by a suitably chosen pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a surface with more than one boundary component.

==Properties==

* If <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> and <math> p\ne 0</math> then <math>\varphi</math> is fully irreducible if and only if <math>\varphi^p</math> is fully irreducible.
*Every fully irreducible <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> can be represented by an expanding irreducible [[train track map]].<ref name="BH92">Mladen Bestvina, and Michael Handel, [https://www.jstor.org/pss/2946562 ''Train tracks and automorphisms of free groups.'']  [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), vol.  135  (1992),  no. 1, pp. 1&ndash;51</ref>
*Every fully irreducible <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> has exponential growth in <math>F_n</math> given by a ''stretch factor'' <math>\lambda=\lambda(\varphi)>1</math>. This [[stretch factor]] has the property that for every free basis <math>X</math> of <math>F_n</math> (and, more generally, for every point of the Culler–Vogtmann [[Outer space (mathematics)|Outer space <math>X\in cv_n</math>]]) and for every <math>1\ne g\in F_n</math> one has:
:: <math>\lim_{k\to\infty}\sqrt[k]{\|\varphi^k(g)\|_X}=\lambda. </math>
Moreover, <math>\lambda=\lambda(\varphi)</math> is equal to the [[Outer space (mathematics)|Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue]] of the transition matrix of any train track representative of <math>\varphi</math>.<ref name="BH92"/><ref>Oleg Bogopolski. [https://books.google.com/books?id=jEw8MpP6DIgC&dq=Oleg+Bogopolski+Introduction+to+Group+Theory&pg=PT1 ''Introduction to group theory''.] EMS Textbooks in Mathematics. [[European Mathematical Society]], Zürich, 2008. {{ISBN|978-3-03719-041-8}}</ref>
*Unlike for stretch factors of pseudo-Anosov surface homeomorphisms, it can happen that for a fully irreducible <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> one has <math> \lambda(\varphi)\ne \lambda(\varphi^{-1})</math><ref>Michael Handel, and Lee Mosher, [https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/2007-359-07/S0002-9947-07-04065-2/S0002-9947-07-04065-2.pdf ''Parageometric outer automorphisms of free groups.''] [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] '''359''' (2007), no. 7, 3153–3183</ref> and this behavior is believed to be generic. However, Handel and Mosher<ref>Michael Handel, Lee Mosher, [https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/2007-359-07/S0002-9947-07-04066-4/S0002-9947-07-04066-4.pdf ''The expansion factors of an outer automorphism and its inverse.'']  [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] '''359''' (2007), no. 7, 3185–3208</ref> proved that for every <math>n\ge 2</math> there exists a finite constant <math>0< C_n <\infty</math> such that for every fully irreducible <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>
:: <math>\frac{\log\lambda(\varphi) }{\log \lambda(\varphi^{-1})} \le C_n.  </math>
*A fully irreducible <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> is ''non-atoroidal'', that is, has a periodic conjugacy class of a nontrivial element of <math>F_n</math>, if and only if <math>\varphi</math> is induced by a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a compact connected surface with one boundary component and with the fundamental group isomorphic to <math>F_n</math>.<ref name="BH92"/>
*A fully irreducible element <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> has exactly two fixed points in the Thurston compactification <math>\overline{CV}_n</math> of the projectivized Outer space <math>CV_n</math>, and <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> acts on <math>\overline{CV}_n</math> with "North-South" dynamics.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Levitt | first1 = Gilbert
 | last2 = Lustig | first2 = Martin
 | title = Automorphisms of free groups have asymptotically periodic dynamics
 | journal = [[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]
 | pages = 1–36
 | volume = 2008
 | year = 2008
 | issue = 619
 | doi=10.1515/CRELLE.2008.038| arxiv = math/0407437
 | s2cid = 14724939
 }}</ref>
*For a fully irreducible element <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>, its fixed points in <math>\overline{CV}_n</math> are projectivized <math>\mathbb R</math>-trees <math>[T_+(\varphi)], [T_-(\varphi)]</math>, where <math>T_+(\varphi),T_-(\varphi)\in \overline{cv}_n</math>, satisfying the property that <math>T_+(\varphi)\varphi=\lambda(\varphi) T_+(\varphi) </math> and <math>T_-(\varphi)\varphi^{-1}=\lambda(\varphi^{-1}) T_-(\varphi) </math>.<ref name=BFH97/>
*A fully irreducible element <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> acts on the space of projectivized geodesic currents <math>\mathbb PCurr(F_n)</math> with either "North-South" or "generalized North-South" dynamics, depending on whether <math>\varphi</math> is atoroidal or non-atoroidal.<ref>Caglar Uyanik, ''Dynamics of hyperbolic iwips''. [[Conformal Geometry and Dynamics]] '''18''' (2014), 192–216.</ref><ref>Caglar Uyanik, ''Generalized north-south dynamics on the space of geodesic currents''. [[Geometriae Dedicata]] '''177''' (2015), 129–148.</ref>
* If <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> is fully irreducible, then the [[commensurator]] <math> Comm(\langle \varphi\rangle)\le \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> is virtually cyclic.<ref>Ilya Kapovich, and Martin Lustig, ''Stabilizers of'' <math>\mathbb{R}</math>-''trees with free isometric actions of F<sub>N</sub>''. 
[[Journal of Group Theory]] '''14''' (2011), no. 5, 673–694.</ref> In particular, the [[centralizer]] and the [[normalizer]] of <math>\langle \varphi\rangle</math> in <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> are virtually cyclic.
*If <math>\varphi,\psi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> are independent fully irreducibles, then <math>[T_\pm(\varphi)], [T_\pm(\psi)]\in \overline{CV}_n</math> are four distinct points, and there exists <math>M\ge 1</math> such that for every <math>p,q\ge M </math> the subgroup <math>\langle \varphi^p, \psi^q\rangle \le \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> is isomorphic to <math>F_2</math>.<ref name=BFH97/> 
* If <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> is fully irreducible and <math>\varphi\in H\le \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>, then either <math>H</math> is virtually cyclic or <math>H</math> contains a subgroup isomorphic to <math>F_2</math>.<ref name=BFH97>Mladen Bestvina, Mark Feighn and Michael Handel, ''Laminations, trees, and irreducible automorphisms of free groups''. [[Geometric and Functional Analysis (journal)|Geometric and Functional Analysis]] '''7''' (1997), 215–244.</ref>  [This statement provides a strong form of the [[Tits alternative]] for subgroups of <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> containing fully irreducibles.]
*If <math>H\le \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> is an arbitrary subgroup, then either <math>H</math> contains a fully irreducible element, or there exist a finite index subgroup <math>H_0\le H</math> and a proper free factor <math>A</math> of <math>F_n</math> such that <math>H_0[A]=[A]</math>.<ref>Camille Horbez,  ''A short proof of Handel and Mosher's alternative for subgroups of'' Out(''F''<sub>''N''</sub>). [[Groups, Geometry, and Dynamics]] '''10''' (2016), no. 2, 709–721.</ref>
* An element <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> acts as a loxodromic isometry on the [[free factor complex]] <math>\mathcal{FF}_n</math> if and only if <math>\varphi</math> is fully irreducible.<ref>Mladen Bestvina, and Mark Feighn, ''Hyperbolicity of the complex of free factors''. [[Advances in Mathematics]] '''256''' (2014), 104–155.</ref>
*It is known that "random" (in the sense of random walks) elements of <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> are fully irreducible. More precisely, if <math>\mu</math> is a measure on <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> whose support generates a semigroup in  <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> containing some two independent fully irreducibles. Then for the random walk of length <math>k</math> on <math>\operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> determined by <math>\mu</math>, the probability that we obtain a fully irreducible element converges to 1 as <math>k\to \infty</math>.<ref>Joseph Maher and Giulio Tiozzo, [https://www.degruyter.com/view/j/crll.ahead-of-print/crelle-2015-0076/crelle-2015-0076.xml ''Random walks on weakly hyperbolic groups''], [[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]], Ahead of print (Jan 2016);   cf. Theorem 1.4</ref>
*A fully irreducible element <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math> admits a (generally non-unique) periodic ''axis'' in the volume-one normalized Outer space <math>X_n</math>, which is geodesic with respect to the asymmetric Lipschitz metric on <math>X_n</math> and possesses strong "contraction"-type properties.<ref>Yael Algom-Kfir,
''Strongly contracting geodesics in outer space''. 
[[Geometry & Topology]] '''15''' (2011), no. 4, 2181–2233.</ref> A related object, defined for an atoroidal fully irreducible <math>\varphi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)</math>, is the ''axis bundle'' <math>A_\varphi\subseteq X_n</math>, which is a certain <math>\varphi</math>-invariant closed subset proper homotopy equivalent to a line.<ref>Michael Handel, and Lee Mosher,
''Axes in outer space.''  [[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]] '''213''' (2011), no. 1004; {{ISBN|978-0-8218-6927-7}}.</ref>
